stem: A postoperative client reports pain of 8/10 and receives an analgesic. Which action best demonstrates appropriate nursing evaluation of the intervention?

options.A: Document the medication as given and wait until the next shift to assess the client's response
options.B: Reassess pain and function at a time appropriate to the medication's route and expected onset or peak, and evaluate for adverse effects
options.C: Reassess only if the client requests another dose because the original pain score already established the need for treatment
options.D: Use changes in heart rate and blood pressure instead of asking the client about pain because physiologic signs are more reliable than self-report

rationale: Evaluation is part of the nursing process. After a pain intervention, the nurse reassesses whether the intervention achieved the client's comfort and functional goals and whether adverse effects occurred. The timing should reflect the route and expected onset/peak rather than an arbitrary universal interval. Self-report remains central when the client can communicate.
educational_objective: Reassess pain, function, and treatment effects after an analgesic at an interval appropriate to the intervention rather than relying on a fixed universal time or physiologic signs alone.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf
source_locator: Comfort — Evaluation: regularly evaluate intervention effectiveness; after analgesics reassess in about an hour or another time frame based on route, onset, and peak; follow up if ineffective
source_claim_supported: Pain interventions require reassessment for effectiveness, with timing individualized to the medication route/onset/peak rather than one universal interval.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort — pain management and nonpharmacological comfort interventions
blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — pain assessment and evaluation
correction_summary: Replaced the low-discrimination 'regularly per protocol' recall item with an applied evaluation question. Removed any universal reassessment minute requirement and tied timing to route/onset/peak while adding function and adverse-effect evaluation.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Reassessment after intervention, route/onset/peak-based timing, function and adverse-effect evaluation are supported.
audit_findings.choice_B: Correct; matches nursing-process evaluation and medication kinetics.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; reassessment is not contingent on a new request.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; physiologic signs do not replace client self-report when available.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B includes timely and comprehensive evaluation.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices describe plausible assessment strategies.
audit_findings.blueprint: Basic Care and Comfort / pain management.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked route-specific timing, opioid/nonopioid differences, self-report hierarchy, and fixed-time overclaim; no unresolved conflict.
